drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Thank you. We propose a $375,000 base salary and 12 months’ base salary plus continued employer contributions toward health benefits for a qualifying termination, subject to a release. We have included a defined good-reason trigger with notice and cure protections. We accept deletion of the non-compete. The intended governing law remains subject to client confirmation; we will revert on that point before execution.

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. The Executive shall receive an annual base salary of $375,000, payable in accordance with the Company's regular payroll practices, and shall be eligible to participate in employee benefit plans generally available to similarly situated executives, subject to their terms.

3. SEVERANCE. Upon termination by the Company without Cause or resignation by the Executive for Good Reason, the Company shall pay the Executive any accrued but unpaid salary and other vested amounts required by applicable law or the applicable benefit plan. In addition, subject to the Executive executing and not revoking a customary release of claims, the Company shall provide (a) severance equal to 12 months of the Executive's then-current base salary, payable in installments over 12 months, and (b) if the Executive timely elects continuation health coverage under applicable law, continued employer contributions toward that coverage on the same basis as immediately before termination for up to 12 months, ending earlier upon eligibility for another employer's health coverage. Good Reason means, without the Executive's written consent, a material reduction in base salary, a material diminution of duties or authority, or relocation of the Executive's principal workplace by more than 50 miles. The Executive must give written notice within 60 days after the condition first arises, allow the Company 30 days to cure, and resign within 30 days after the cure period expires if the condition remains uncured.
Define Cause in the next draft and confirm severance payment and release mechanics comply with applicable law, including Section 409A if applicable.
